explanations.A: Stenosis of the cerebral aqueduct is the commonest cause of congenital obstructive hydrocephalus, but it dilates the lateral and third ventricles while leaving the fourth ventricle small - the opposite of the MRI finding here.
explanations.B: Dandy-Walker malformation results from failure of development of the outlet foramina of Luschka and Magendie, so cerebrospinal fluid cannot escape from the fourth ventricle. explanations.C: Excess cerebrospinal fluid production is characteristic of a choroid plexus papilloma, which shows an intraventricular mass, not a cystic posterior fossa with an absent vermis.

questions.question: Which of the following statements holds true for inactivated (killed) vaccines?
options: They never need a booster dose
They usually need booster doses to sustain immunity
They confer lifelong immunity with no boosters
They work only when given as a single dose
questions.explanation: Correct. Killed organisms cannot replicate in the host, so the antigenic stimulus is limited to what is injected and the resulting antibody response is weaker and shorter-lived than that from a live vaccine. A primary series of several doses is therefore needed to establish protection, followed by boosters to maintain titres. Adjuvants are often added for the same reason.

explanations.A: Boosters are in fact routine for this class. The immunising schedules for DPT, IPV, hepatitis B and rabies all build in repeat doses.
explanations.B: Correct. Killed organisms cannot replicate in the host, so the antigenic stimulus is limited to what is injected and the resulting antibody response is weaker and shorter-lived than that from a live vaccine. A primary series of several doses is therefore needed to establish protection, followed by boosters to maintain titres. Adjuvants are often added for the same reason.
explanations.C: Durable, sometimes lifelong immunity after one or two doses is characteristic of live attenuated vaccines such as measles or BCG, in which the organism multiplies and mimics natural infection. Killed vaccines behave differently.
explanations.D: A single dose of a killed vaccine seldom produces protective immunity; it primes the immune system, and subsequent doses generate the protective response.

questions.question: Some weeks into anti-tubercular treatment that includes isoniazid, a 45-year-old man reports that both his hands and feet feel numb and keep tingling. Which nursing action takes priority?
options: Give vitamin B12 supplementation
Raise the isoniazid dose
Give vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) supplementation
Stop isoniazid at once
questions.explanation: This is the correct action. Isoniazid competes with pyridoxine and increases its urinary loss, depleting pyridoxal-5-phosphate and producing a symmetrical distal sensory neuropathy. Pyridoxine 10 mg daily is given prophylactically to those at risk (malnourished, diabetic, alcohol-dependent, pregnant, HIV-positive), and 50-100 mg daily once neuropathy has appeared. Treatment for tuberculosis continues alongside.

explanations.A: Cobalamin deficiency does cause a peripheral neuropathy, but the mechanism here is entirely different. Giving B12 leaves the underlying pyridoxine depletion uncorrected and the symptoms will persist.
explanations.B: Escalating the dose is the opposite of what is required. Neuropathy from isoniazid is dose-related, so a higher dose would deepen the deficiency and worsen the sensory symptoms.
explanations.C: This is the correct action. Isoniazid competes with pyridoxine and increases its urinary loss, depleting pyridoxal-5-phosphate and producing a symmetrical distal sensory neuropathy. Pyridoxine 10 mg daily is given prophylactically to those at risk (malnourished, diabetic, alcohol-dependent, pregnant, HIV-positive), and 50-100 mg daily once neuropathy has appeared. Treatment for tuberculosis continues alongside.
explanations.D: Abrupt withdrawal of a first-line drug interrupts an effective regimen and risks acquired resistance. Isoniazid is discontinued only if the neuropathy is severe or fails to respond after adequate pyridoxine; it is not the first response to mild paraesthesiae.

questions.question: A population's age-sex pyramid is drawn with a broad base that tapers sharply to a very narrow apex. What does a profile of this shape indicate about that population?

explanations.C: A low birth rate with high mortality would give a narrow base as well as a narrow top, producing a contracting or constrictive shape rather than the broad-based triangle described.

questions.question: A preterm baby in the NICU is being watched for hypoxia. Of the manifestations listed, which one appears LATE in the course?
options: Tachypnea
Nasal flaring
Cyanosis
Restlessness
questions.explanation: Cyanosis is a late and unreliable sign. Visible blue discolouration requires roughly 5 g/dL of desaturated haemoglobin in the capillary bed, so it appears only after oxygenation has fallen substantially, and it can be masked altogether in an anaemic infant or exaggerated in polycythaemia. Central cyanosis of the tongue and mucous membranes is the significant form; peripheral acrocyanosis in the first day or two of life is normal. Pulse oximetry and blood gases detect the problem long before the colour changes.

Immediately discontinue HFNC and switch to BVM with 100% oxygen
Reposition the child prone and reassess SpO2 after 15 minutes
questions.explanation: Critical hypoxaemia demands immediate positive-pressure ventilation with a bag-valve-mask on 100% oxygen with a reservoir, while help is called and the cause is sought. explanations.A: Adding flow only titrates a device that has already failed. At an SpO2 of 50% the child has minutes of reserve, and bradycardia followed by cardiac arrest is the next step in the paediatric deterioration sequence.
explanations.B: Summoning another professional before delivering oxygen delays rescue ventilation. The nurse at the bedside must ventilate first and call for help simultaneously.
explanations.C: Critical hypoxaemia demands immediate positive-pressure ventilation with a bag-valve-mask on 100% oxygen with a reservoir, while help is called and the cause is sought. explanations.D: A 15-minute wait at an SpO2 of 50% is indefensible; hypoxic bradycardia and arrest would occur long before the reassessment.
